title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Drafting Studio. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Drafting Studio
options.lineage: engineering drawing sets and the working architect's studio
options.thesis: A photoreal engineer's studio in late daylight, where the work is issued as a drawing set.
materials: birch ply, concrete and plaster under low sun
options.viewport: Wide daylight shot of the studio: sun shafts across a drafting desk, the laptop the sharpest thing in frame.
options.risk: The drawing-set grammar on the laptop reads as costume unless the title block and sheet index actually navigate.

raised.raise: The loader counts real asset progress to 100 instead of a static line.
The laptop's sheet index always marks where you are, like a chase light.
Every sheet is deep-linkable (#projects) so a recruiter can share the exact page.

options.label: Archviz Loft
options.thesis: A Scandinavian loft rendered like an archviz still: low sun, white oak, linen, plaster.
options.viewport: Sunlit loft corner with the desk by a tall window; the laptop carries a calm, native-feeling desktop.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most 'make the room realistic' runs land.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A full-screen shader with thin type floating over living pixels.
options.viewport: One huge word over a breathing shader; corner links.
options.case: Fuses poorly: throws away the realistic room you asked for, and recruiters lose the obvious path to content.
options.kept: A loader that counts real progress.
options.risk: Style over substance for a hiring audience.

options.label: Rhythm Machine
options.thesis: Sections as a sixteen-step row under a running chase light.
options.viewport: A step row as the page's one unbroken line.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to a developer's work or to realism.
options.kept: An always-visible marker of where you are.

options.label: Folding Sequence
options.thesis: One sheet folded through numbered, recoverable steps.
options.viewport: A centred sheet with numbered folds in a margin column.
options.case: Fuses poorly: beautiful, but recruiters don't identify with it and it drops the room.
options.risk: Reads as an art piece, not a portfolio.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Projects as numbered exploded assembly steps.
options.viewport: Big step numeral, ghosted prior assembly, bright new piece.
options.kept: Wordless arrows: the laptop affordance should be a cue, not a paragraph.
options.risk: Playful where the brief asks for professional.

options.label: Rental Wall
options.thesis: Projects as clamshell spines on a genre wall.
options.viewport: A packed shelf, one box pulled face-out.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nostalgic theme, no realism, wrong audience.
options.kept: Browsing sideways along a shelf is a strong physical metaphor for a project list.

options.label: Signal Degradation
options.thesis: Colour bars and a crawl, tuned like channels.
options.case: Fuses poorly: glitch aesthetics fight 'professional and realistic'.
options.kept: A live clock locked to one corner of the laptop.

canonCard.label: Cozy night bedroom, done right
canonCard.thesis: The lo-fi night bedroom with fairy lights and a glowing laptop, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Same room as today, re-lit and re-textured to a much higher standard.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from most 3D-room portfolios by design.
